title: Model polynomials with algebra tiles (x², x and unit tiles, positive and negative) and read the expression from a tile picture

lesson.title: Reading Polynomials from Algebra Tiles

steps.say: You already know how to name a polynomial by its terms and coefficients, and you have pushed algebra tiles around to solve equations like three x minus four equals negative thirteen. Today we do one small thing: build a polynomial out of tiles, and read a polynomial straight off a tile picture.

There are only three tile sizes, and each one is an area. The big square is x long and x wide, so its area is x times x, which is x squared. The long strip is x long and one wide, so its area is x. The small square is one by one, so it is worth one. Colour tells you the sign: shaded means positive, white means negative.

visual.caption: Imagine the side is x (not 3): the whole square is like an x² tile, the shaded strip is like an x tile, one cell is like a unit tile.

steps.say: Let us read a tile picture. Say you see two shaded big squares, three shaded strips, and four white small squares. Count each size on its own. Two x squared tiles give two x squared. Three x tiles give three x. Four white unit tiles are negative, so they give minus four. Put it together: two x squared plus three x minus four. That is a trinomial with coefficients two and three and a constant term of negative four.

Here is a mistake I see a lot: reading one big square as two x. It looks tempting because there is a two in x squared. But the exponent two means x times x, the area of a square, while two x means two strips side by side. Test it with a number. If x were three, the big square has area nine, but two strips only cover six. Different sizes, different meaning. One big square is always x squared.

visual.caption: With x = 3: the square covers 9, two strips cover only 6

steps.say: Second mistake: leaving a zero pair in the answer. Picture one shaded big square, four shaded strips, two white strips, and three white units. A shaded strip and a white strip are plus x and minus x, and together they cancel to zero. Two white strips cancel two of the shaded ones, leaving two shaded strips. So the polynomial is x squared plus two x minus three, not x squared plus four x minus two x minus three. Always cancel zero pairs before you write the expression.

visual.caption: 4 positive x tiles, 2 negative x tiles → 2 zero pairs cancel → 2x left

steps.say: So here is the whole step in one line. Big square is x squared, strip is x, small square is one. Shaded is positive, white is negative. Count each size, cancel zero pairs, and write the terms from biggest tile to smallest.

lesson.answer: Big square = x², strip = x, small square = 1; shaded is positive, white is negative. Count each size, cancel zero pairs, write the polynomial.

practice.question: Draw this tile picture yourself: two shaded x squared tiles, five shaded x tiles, two white x tiles, and three white unit tiles. Cancel any zero pairs, then write the polynomial the picture shows.
practice.answer: The two white x tiles cancel two of the shaded x tiles, leaving three x tiles. The polynomial is 2x² + 3x − 3.
